title: Life at the limit: the tardigrade
text: Under a microscope, a drop of damp moss reveals eight-legged animals affectionately known {{1}} water bears. Tardigrades {{2}} found on every continent, from mountain tops to the deep sea, yet the situations {{3}} they truly excel are the extremes: vacuum, radiation and deep freeze. {{4}} is this resilience that has made them the celebrities of the microscopic world. In 2007, {{5}} a small colony travelled into orbit, the animals were exposed directly to the vacuum of space — and returned {{6}} apparent ease. Many survive {{7}} water for a decade by expelling almost all of their moisture and suspending their metabolism, and they are not quite insects, {{8}} are they microbes; they belong to an ancient lineage of their own.

gaps.explanation: Present passive with a plural subject: tardigrades are found.

gaps.hint: relative adverb: the situations ___ they excel
gaps.explanation: 'Where' refers back to situations; a plain 'that' would leave the clause without an adverb.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ is this resilience that
gaps.explanation: The cleft structure 'It is X that Y' emphasises resilience.

gaps.hint: time relative: in 2007, ___ a colony travelled
gaps.explanation: Non-defining time clause after the year: 'in 2007, when…'.
'With' + abstract noun expresses manner: with apparent ease.
'Without water' — the state they endure is the absence of water.

gaps.hint: correlative: not quite insects, ___ are they microbes
gaps.explanation: 'Nor' continues a negative clause with inversion: nor are they…
